motion.name: micro-loop-wave

motion.name: hover-lift

narrative.northStar: The group chat, grown to page scale.
narrative.overview:
FreedomTalk's landing is a flat, playful charcoal world pinned to the Discord design language: a dark ground ramp that steps brighter as panels stack, one blurple that owns every action, and a loud sticker palette that lives only inside artwork. Chunky rounded display type (Baloo 2) shouts the message; a clean rounded body face (Nunito) carries the prose. Bird-mascot characters and flat mockups of the actual app — chat windows, friends lists, voice rooms — are drawn as authored vector scenes, so the page feels like the product rather than a screenshot of it.

This system exists only inside the .ftl namespace in landing.css. Every token is prefixed --ftl-* and every rule is nested under .ftl. The shared app/globals.css (warm-charcoal/amber world) still serves the auth and chat pages and must stay untouched — do not unify the two worlds, promote .ftl tokens to :root, or style other surfaces with them.

The system is flat-first, confirmed by the shipped code: zero box-shadow drop shadows, zero gradients, zero backdrop-filter glass, zero photography. Depth is tonal (surface color steps), closeness is corner radius, and liveliness is motion plus artwork. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce every animation is off and all content is visible.
keyCharacteristics: Charcoal ground ramp (#23272a → #2c2f33 → #36393f, hairlines #3d4046, footer band #111214) with near-white ink in four steps.
One action color: blurple #5865f2 for fills, selection, and accent words; deep indigo #31368e as its hover depth.
Sticker palette (yellow/fuchsia/green/red) confined to artwork and micro-accents, never structural fills.
Flat everywhere: color-swap button hovers with a 2px lift, no shadow vocabulary.
Rounded, capsule-driven shapes: 12px controls up to 32px hero panels, 9999px pills.
One ambient motion moment (the hero scene); sections settle once and only when JS can reveal them.

rules.name: The Scoped World Rule
rules.body: This system exists only inside the `.ftl` namespace in `packages/web/components/landing/landing.css`. Every token is prefixed `--ftl-*` and every rule is nested under `.ftl`. The shared `app/globals.css` (warm-charcoal/amber world) still serves the auth and chat pages and must stay untouched — do not "unify" the two worlds, promote `.ftl` tokens to `:root`, or style other surfaces with them.

rules.name: The Sticker Containment Rule
rules.body: Sticker colors never fill structure. No yellow buttons, no fuchsia panels, no green sections. Outside artwork they surface only as micro-accents: the yellow hover-underline, the yellow "Open source" badge and button focus ring, the green BETA chip. If a proposed element puts a sticker color on a background larger than a chip, it's breaking the world.

rules.name: The Red Rule
rules.body: #ed4245 is window-chrome art material, not UI. It must not appear on buttons, text, badges, or state colors outside a drawn app window.

rules.name: The One Blurple Phrase Rule
rules.body: On a charcoal ground, exactly one phrase inside a display headline takes blurple ("fun & games" in the H1); everything else stays near-white. On the blurple CTA panel the headline is entirely white — no accent word.

rules.name: The Flat Ground Rule
rules.body: Surfaces never cast shadows. If a design needs separation, step the surface color up the ramp or add a hairline; if it needs emphasis, use blurple, radius, or motion. Inset rings may impersonate borders; drop shadows and glass may not enter.

rules.name: The Wrapper Rule
rules.body: An animation class never shares an SVG element with a `transform` attribute; animated art is wrapped in a class-bearing `<g>` around the transformed child. Voice/typing elements that do animate directly set `transform-box: fill-box` and skip transform attributes.

dos: Do keep all landing styling inside the `.ftl` namespace with `--ftl-*` tokens; load `landing.css` only from the landing page.
Do make every interactive target at least 48px tall (44px for the compact nav variant) and give buttons color-swap hovers plus the 2px lift.
Do mark decorative SVGs `aria-hidden` and give meaningful scenes a `role="img"` + label (the hero scene is labeled; sprinkles are hidden).
Do keep stickers bare — flat solid fills with no outlines, filled or line-art alike (`stroke="#ffffff"` outlines are banned on artwork; partial strokes read as glitches).
Do optically center artwork contents: an initial's baseline sits at circle-center + 0.35 × font-size; icons in pills center on the pill midline with a clear gap before their label.
Do write real product microcopy into drawn UI — real channel names, messages, presence states from the shipped feature set.
Do draw depth with the tonal ramp and hairlines, and reserve blurple for actions and one accent phrase.
donts: Don't apply sticker colors (yellow/fuchsia/green/red) as fills on structural UI — they belong in artwork and chip-scale accents only.
Don't introduce drop shadows, glass/backdrop-filter, gradients, or stock photography; this world is flat by audit and by doctrine.
Don't use red anywhere except inside drawn window chrome, and don't let sticker colors touch buttons, text fills, or section backgrounds.
Don't merge `.ftl` tokens into `globals.css`, restyle the auth/chat pages with them, or "upgrade" the old world — the split is deliberate.
Don't put an animation class on the same SVG element that carries a `transform` attribute, and don't add new looping animation outside the hero scene.
Don't hide content behind scroll reveals without the JS-armed pattern — unrevealed sections must be visible with JavaScript disabled.
